The '''2012–13 Scottish Premier League''' was the fifteenth and final season of the [[Scottish Premier League]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]], since its inception in 1998. The season began on 4 August 2012<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16293107 | title=Scottish Premier League sets 4 August start date for 2012/13 season | publisher=BBC Sport | date=21 December 2011 | access-date=7 April 2012}}</ref> and ended on 19 May 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotprem.com/content/default.asp?page=s49 | title=Key dates | publisher=Scottish Premier League | access-date=16 June 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130705063057/http://www.scotprem.com/content/default.asp?page=s49 | archive-date=5 July 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Twelve teams contested the league. [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] (champions) and [[Dundee FC|Dundee]] (runners-up) were promoted from the [[2011–12 Scottish First Division|2011–12 First Division]], replacing [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]] (relegated) and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] (now in the Third Division). After the SPL clubs voted against the new Rangers company replacing the old Rangers company in the league,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18703183#:~:text=Rangers%20will%20not%20play%20in,and%20Rangers%20voting%20in%20favour./ |title=Rival teams block Rangers from playing in Scottish Premier League |work=BBC News |date=4 July 2012 |access-date=3 May 2025}}</ref> the club were accepted into the [[Scottish Football League Third Division|fourth tier]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11788/7897300/rangers-put-in-third-division |title=Rangers demoted to 3rd division after debt crisis |work=SkySports News |date=13 July 2012 |access-date=3 May 2025}}</ref> with Dundee taking their place in the SPL.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/jul/16/dundee-replace-rangers-spl |title=Dundee replace Rangers in SPL |work=The Guardian|date=16 July 2012 |access-date=22 November 2020}}</ref>

On 21 April, Celtic retained their title after a 4–1 home win against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] at [[Celtic Park]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Martin |last=Conaghan |title=Celtic 4–1 Inverness CT |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22141268 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 April 2013 |access-date=21 April 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/203492.html#|title= Celtic retain Scottish Premier League title|date=21 April 2013|publisher=ESPN|access-date=22 April 2013 }}</ref>

This was the final season of the Scottish Premier League before it was abolished in June 2013, when the SPL and SFL merged to form the new [[Scottish Professional Football League]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22864944|title=Scottish Football League clubs vote in favour of a proposed merger with the Scottish Premier League.|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=2013-06-12}}</ref> with its top division being known as the [[Scottish Premiership]].

[[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]] were relegated from the 2011–12 Scottish Premier League. [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], who won the [[2011–12 Scottish First Division]], were promoted. The 2012–13 season marks the top-flight debut for the Highland team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18498399|title=Ross County ready for Scotland's top-flight|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 June 2012|access-date=18 June 2012}}</ref>

After [[Administration and liquidation of The Rangers Football Club plc| failing to exit administration by an agreed CVA]], [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] was replaced with the term "Club 12" when the fixture list was published on 18 June 2012.<ref name = "club 12"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18484588|title=Rangers replaced with 'Club 12' in SPL fixture list|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 June 2012|access-date=18 June 2012}}</ref> The transfer of the club's membership share of the SPL to the new company that had bought Rangers was dependent on a vote by the remaining SPL clubs.<ref name = "club 12">{{cite news| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/rangers/9337279/Rangers-would-have-to-start-in-Scottish-League-Division-Three-says-SFL-chief-executive-David-Longmuir.html | title=Rangers would have to start in Scottish League Division Three |first=Ewing|last=Grahame|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=London | date=17 June 2012 | access-date=17 June 2012}}</ref> Eight clubs publicly declared that they would oppose the membership transfer, which would mean that they could not play in the SPL.<ref>{{cite news|title=Newco Rangers will not get votes for SPL transfer|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18577192|date=25 June 2012|access-date=25 June 2012|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> The vote took place on 4 July 2012, and Rangers were refused re-entry to the SPL by a 10-1 majority.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.itv.com/news/update/2012-07-04/rival-teams-block-rangers-from-playing-in-scottish-premier-league/ |title=Rival teams block Rangers from playing in Scottish Premier League |work=ITV News |date=4 July 2012 |access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="Vote">{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18703183 | title=Rangers newco refused SPL entry after chairmen vote | publisher=BBC Sport | date=4 July 2012 | access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref> [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], who had finished second in the 2011–12 Scottish First Division, were invited to replace Rangers.<ref name = "Vote"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18850864 |publisher=BBC Sport|title=Rangers: Dundee invited to take place in SPL |access-date=28 July 2012|date=16 July 2012}}</ref>

===Scoring===
*First goal of the season: [[Kris Commons]] for Celtic against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] (<small>''4 August 2012''</small>)
*Fastest goal of the season: ''' 12 seconds''', [[Kris Commons]] for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] (<small>''16 March 2013''</small>)<ref>{{cite news | title  =Celtic 4–Aberdeen 3 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21724379|publisher=BBC Sport  |date=2 September 2012 |access-date=19 January 2013}}</ref>
*Latest goal of the season: '''94 minutes''', [[Georgios Samaras]] for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] (<small>''16 March 2013''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=Celtic 4–3 Aberdeen |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21724379|publisher=BBC Sport  |date=16 March 2013 |access-date=16 March 2013}}</ref>
*Largest winning margin: '''5 goals'''
**St Mirren 0–5 Celtic (<small>''20 October 2012''</small>)
**Celtic 5–0 Dundee (<small>''24 February 2013''</small>)
*Highest scoring game: '''9 goals'''
**St Mirren 5–4 Ross County (<small>''29 September 2012''</small>)
*Most goals scored in a match by a single team: '''6 goals'''
**Celtic 6–2 Dundee United (<small>''16 February 2013''</small>)
*Most goals scored in a match by a losing team: '''4 goals'''
**St Mirren 5–4 Ross County (<small>''29 September 2012''</small>)
